question.text: This early 19th century Zulu monarch developed the "bull horn" formation and a shorter style of spear as part of his massive military reformation. The expansion of his realm is argued to have triggered the Mfecane (m-fay-thaa-nay), a long period of social upheaval in southern Africa.
question.clue: Mfecane resulted when the tribes nearby attempted to escape this man's forces, and he was assassinated by his brother Dingane.

swap.leadin: In a "Free State" with this name, the Force Publique terrorized workers extracting rubber.
swap.text: Give the name of that colony personally owned by Leopold II. The colony shared this name with two modern-day nations led from Kinshasa and Brazzaville.
swap.answerHtml: Congo [accept Congo Free State or Republic of the Congo or Democratic Republic of the Congo]
swap.clue: In a colony with this name, the Force Publique cut off the hands of native laborers who did not meet their rubber quotas.

question.text: The most famous ruler of Mali was this man. His general Sagmandia conquered Gao, and his own accomplishments include founding Sankore University and debasing the value of gold in Egypt during his hajj.
question.clue: This person was depicted holding a fleur-de-lys and a golden orb by Abraham Cresques on the Atlas of Catalan.

swap.text: Gaddafi led this North African country, which disputed the Aouzou Strip with its southern neighbor, Chad. The U.S. embassy in this country's city of Benghazi was attacked in 2012.
swap.clue: This country's city of Sirte is controlled by ISIS.

question.text: The Moroccan explorer Leo Africanus wrote of the fabulous wealth of this Malian city, while Europeans often considered it to be a fantastical, faraway location.
question.clue: The Frenchman Rene Caillie was the first European to return alive from visiting this city.

swap.leadin: Eight carvings of soapstone eagles from this city's ruins are the basis for its country's national emblem.
swap.text: Name this city, which contains many large stone structures. It was built by the ancestors of the Shona people.
swap.answerHtml: Great Zimbabwe [do NOT accept or prompt on “Zimbabwe”]
swap.clue: A soapstone bird excavated at this site is a symbol of its modern-day country, and this site was ruled by kings titled monomotapa.

question.text: This Ethiopian emperor presided over the victory at Adowa.
question.clue: This son of Haile Malakot took the name of the legendary son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

swap.leadin: A conflict in this country's capital was dramatized in a film by Gillo Pontecorvo.
swap.text: Name this country. Its independence led to widespread reprisals against loyalists called harkis, as well as a mass exodus of Europeans nicknamed "black feet."
swap.answerHtml: People’s Democratic Republic of Algeria (accept République algérienne démocratique et populaire)
swap.clue: After the exile of its ruler, Hussien Dey, Abdel Kadir led a rebellion in this nation.

question.text: Rising in the thirteenth century, it founded Lagos under Ewuare the Great and engaged in large-scale human sacrifices until its capital was burned by British forces in 1897. Its obas still advise politicians in the present-day country of the same name.
question.clue: This Kingdom produced many mostly brass namesake "Bronzes."

swap.leadin: Name these entities from African nationalism.
swap.text: Since leading Zimbabwe to independence and economic ruin, this man has launched Operation Drive Out Trash, in which thousands of urban poor had their homes bulldozed.
swap.clue: This leader's G-40-backed wife and a military-backed member of the ZANU both vied to succeed him as president after a 2017 coup.

question.text: This ethnic group attempted to establish the Orange Free State and the Transvaal Republic. They descended from the early Dutch settlers who came to the Cape of Good Hope.
question.clue: Some argue that this African ethnic group's expansionist political aspirations originate with their ancestors' fervent Calvinism. The influence of the Freemasons is often compared to a "Brotherhood" of this ethnic group.

swap.text: The Nigerian Civil War was fought over the secession of this short-lived republic of mostly Igbo peoples from 1967-70.
swap.clue: This country became landlocked after the capture of Port Harcourt, making it harder to alleviate an epidemic of kwashiorkor sweeping this country.

question.text: The attack was perpetrated by this militant Islamist group, whose name means "the youth."
question.clue: This Somali militant group affiliated with al-Qaeda instituted environmental regulations such as banning plastic bags and logging rare species of trees. Its name translates to "the youth," and it has often come in conflict with the Sufi group Ahlu-Sunna-Waljama'a.

swap.leadin: This ethnic group's period of expansion in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries is known as the "Emutai."
swap.text: Name this Nilotic ethnic group whose youths prove themselves as men by single-handedly hunting a lion.
swap.clue: The British punished the Nandi by handing over 10,000 of their cattle to these people. These traditionally pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania subsisted almost entirely on the blood, meat, and milk of their cows.

question.text: If created, this proposed African country would have its capital at Arusha and contain over 300 million people. The "community" of countries that would be in this country is led by Uhuru Kenyatta.

swap.leadin: This politician broke with Goukouni Oueddei's FROLINAT rebels amidst Muammar Qaddafi's invasion of his country's mineral-rich Aouzou Strip.
swap.text: Name this president who led Chad for most of the 1980s, before he was ousted in a coup led by Idriss Deby. His regime's massacres of the Hadjerai and Zaghawa led to his conviction of human rights violations by the ICJ in 2016.
swap.clue: Operations Manta and Epervier supported this man, whose technicals won the Battle of Fada.

question.leadin: In the Women's War of 1929, the people of this ethnic group revolted in response to European attempts to levy taxes based on their female population.
question.text: Name these peoples who celebrate the New Yam Festival and founded the Nri Kingdom.
question.clue: Izuogo Mgbokpo and Chief Iheme were among the leaders of one of their subgroups, the Aro, who formed a vast slave-trading confederacy in western Africa that was wiped out by the British in 1902.

swap.leadin: In the 14th century, this state's sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman built what was then the largest building in sub-Saharan Africa, the coral Palace of Husuni Kubwa.
swap.text: Name this sultanate that dominated the cities of the Swahili Coast in the 15th century. It was legendarily founded by the Persian prince Ali ibn al-Hassan on an island off the coast of Tanzania.
swap.clue: Much of this city's wealth derived from the tribute in gold paid to it by its southern neighbor Sofala.

question.leadin: This dynasty ended when the Merenids captured Marrakech.
question.text: Name this North African Islamic dynasty whose caliph Abu Yaqub Yusuf captured Seville in 1172. They were driven back to Africa after losing the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa.
question.clue: This dynasty's distinctive combination of Zahiri jurisprudence and Ashʿari theology was formalized under its first politically established leader, ʿAbd al-Muʾmin.

swap.leadin: He signed the 1996 Abidjan Agreement with Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, which had little effect on the ongoing civil war.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Revolutionary United Front who was to be tried for war crimes committed during the Sierra Leone civil war before his 2003 death from a stroke.
